verdicts.why: assistant.py:31 puts an unbounded `\S*` inside the negative lookahead, so `.beacon.internal` anywhere in the non-space run kills the match; I ran the pattern and `https://evil.example/abcdef0123456789?x=.beacon.internal` does not match while the same URL without the marker does.

reconcile.py:70-72 logs d.tenant_id and d.account with %s, and those values come straight from csv.DictReader rows at reconcile.py:45-46 with no newline/CR stripping, into logging.basicConfig's one-record-per-line output (consumer.py-style handler set in main).

apply_grants.sql:17 is `reader_by_target.get(target.name, "public")`, and lines 20-21 then `grant usage`/`grant select` to that name, so any target not in the three-entry map hands the relation to the PUBLIC pseudo-role; dbt resolves target names from whatever profiles.yml is in use, not only the three in the repo copy.

client.ts:70-75 retries against PROFILE.fallbackBase passing `[]` as the pins argument at line 74, while the primary call at line 64 passes PROFILE.certificatePins (two real pins in the production profile, env.ts:32-35), so the retry runs unpinned.

AndroidManifest.xml:62-66 declares AttachmentProvider exported=true with grantUriPermissions and no android:permission or path-permission, and AttachmentSync.kt:34-37 builds the file as File(attachmentDir, uri.lastPathSegment) — a percent-encoded segment such as `..%2F..%2Fdatabases%2Fx` decodes into the segment and escapes the directory.
consumer.py:69-72 HMACs only `body`, then line 75 takes `type` from the unsigned stream field, and process() at consumer.py:89 selects the handler from that same msg["type"].

retry.py:37-43 rebuilds the message with _entry_to_message (no HMAC check, unlike consumer.decode:69-72) and calls handlers._apply_payout directly, which per handlers.py:42-43 assumes authorisation was already done — no _require_scope is invoked anywhere on this path.

consumer.js:28 wires ledger.post.v1 to makeLedgerPostingHandler without the idempotency object that line 29-30 passes to the payout handler, and ledgerPosting.js:19-38 has no dedupe — applyPosting (ledger.js:30-39) inserts a new posting row and adds to the balance every time, on an at-least-once Redis stream.
attachments.ts:42 takes workOrderId from the multipart form and line 56-63 inserts it with actor.orgId; there is no query against work_orders to confirm the order exists in the caller's org.

site.yml:24-28 re-downloads stanchion_artifact_mirror with no checksum: key and line 30-36 unarchives it, and the rescue covers the app role whose only integrity gate is the checksum at roles/app/tasks/main.yml:26; ansible.cfg:16-18 makes every task run become root.

consumer.js:30 registers payout.release.v2, but EVENT_SCHEMAS (schema.js:27-52) only defines v1, and validatePayload returns null — i.e. no error — when validatorFor finds no validator (schema.js:68-73), so the v2 payload reaches the money-moving handler unchecked.

index.ts:37 calls .listen(Number(PORT ?? 3000)) with no hostname, which binds 0.0.0.0, while edge.conf:7,10 documents the upstream as loopback-only; auth.ts:19-28 derives the actor (subject, account, roles) from x-forwarded-* headers that only the edge is trusted to overwrite (edge.conf:44-46), so a direct connection forges any identity including ops-admin.
router.ts:46 pushes state.returnTo through assertAllowedRoute, but line 47 passes state.params — parsed from the same attacker-supplied JSON at line 45 — into nav.navigate with no validation at all.

reconcile.py:56 writes the balance key with a bare redis SET of d.theirs_cents, never touching ledger.post_entry whose overdraw guard lives at ledger.py:65-69; the value comes from int(row["closing_cents"]) at reconcile.py:47 with no bound, no tenant/account pattern check and no authorization.

ingest.py:123 does `Document(**message["doc"])` on a plain dataclass, so the DocumentIn validators — the acl_groups wildcard rejection (ingest.py:38-44), the tenant pattern and the body size limit (ingest.py:35,46-51) — are all skipped on this queue path, unlike ingest_upload at line 92.

0007_case_notes.py:29-45 unconditionally inserts firm_demo and prn_demo in upgrade(), and grep over quarrystore/ finds 'demo' nowhere else — the 'skipped by every production query filter' claimed at line 27-28 does not exist; session.py:34-49 only narrows by the current_firm contextvar.

mask_pii.sql:33 is sha256 over `customer_id || pii_policy_version` with no secret salt, and pii_policy_version is the literal 'v3' checked into dbt_project.yml:18, so the digest over a low-entropy id is trivially rebuildable.

config/default.json:21 sets signature.mode to 'warn' so verifySignature returns true even on mismatch (signing.js:38-45), consumer.js:60 therefore admits the forged entry, validatePayload is a no-op for payout.release.v2 (schema.js:68-73), and payoutRelease.js:28 calls ledger.adjustBalance, which has no solvency or ceiling check (ledger.js:59-65).
SessionStore.kt:62 `fun tokenFor(host: String): String? = store().getString(KEY_TOKEN, null)` never reads `host`, so the API's promise of a per-host bearer is not implemented.

search.py:34 interpolates `needle` into a single-quoted SQL literal inside a text() f-string; escape_like (search.py:13-17) only escapes % and _, not the quote, so a term containing ' breaks out — contrast search_docket at line 56, which binds the same value as a parameter.

tools.py:20-26 http_get fetches any URL the model names with no scheme or host allow-list, it is registered in TOOL_SPECS/TOOL_REGISTRY (tools.py:64-94), prompt.py:15-18 instructs the model to use it, and app.py:117-121 feeds the 4000-char response body back into the loop whose final text is returned to the caller at app.py:110-114 — reachable by anyone holding an API key, including the constant demo key in settings.py:47.

chunker.py:23 strips tags with TAG_RE and keeps whatever was inside them, so text in a display:none element becomes ordinary prose in the chunk; the whole function (lines 21-26) does no NFKC normalisation and no zero-width/bidi/control stripping, and chunk() at line 38 is the only path from doc.body to the index (ingest.py:66).

pulsegate-api/package.json:12-18 uses ^ ranges, and so do tallyflow-consumer/package.json:12-17 and harborlight-mobile/package.json:11-23, while beaconindex/pyproject.toml:6-12 and quarrystore/pyproject.toml:6-12 use >=; a find over corpus-v10 for package-lock.json / yarn.lock / bun.lockb / poetry.lock / uv.lock / requirements*.txt returns nothing.

storage.ts:50-68 attaches a Principal '*' s3:GetObject policy when publicExports is set, and Pulumi.staging.yaml:9 sets publicExports true while line 12 sets replicateProdExports true, which storage.ts:70-89 turns into an inbound replication policy from the prod export role.

storage.ts:42-48 sets all four BucketPublicAccessBlock flags to !args.publicExports, i.e. all false in staging (Pulumi.staging.yaml:9), alongside the anonymous ReadExports policy at lines 51-67 and the prod replication policy at lines 73-89 enabled by Pulumi.staging.yaml:12.
reconcile.py:70-72 writes tenant_id and account into a single logging record with no CR/LF neutralisation, and those fields come unfiltered from the scheme's CSV at reconcile.py:45-46.
accounts.ts:74-77 declares `members: t.Array(t.Object(...))` with no maxItems/minItems, and the handler at lines 65-71 loops the whole array issuing one insertMember round trip per row.

attachments.ts:62 stores `file.type` from the multipart upload with no allow-list (only a fallback to application/octet-stream), and attachments.ts:102 echoes that stored value back as the response content-type on download.

consumer.py:38-41 computes the HMAC over the body string alone and consumer.py:69-72 compares only that, while the routing field is read from the unsigned entry at line 75 and drives HANDLERS.get at line 89.

The interpolation at ledgerPosting.js:35 is real, but the handler is registered only for ledger.post.v1 (consumer.js:28), whose payload schema pins currency to the four-value enum with additionalProperties:false (schema.js:8,30-38), and consumer.js:66-71 rejects the message to the DLQ before dispatch if that validator fails — so no attacker-shaped string can reach the sink.

workorders.ts:123 checks only wo.orgId !== actor.orgId, whereas the list at workorders.ts:60-70 narrows by visibleCrewFilter (policy.ts:47-50, crewIds for a tech); and grep shows requireRole (auth.ts:81) is defined but referenced by no route in the project.

policy.ts:18-23 is a module-level object literal whose doc comment (lines 14-17) claims it is loaded at boot and refreshed nightly; grep over fieldops-api finds crewSites referenced only at policy.ts:40 for reads, with no writer, loader or refresh anywhere.

endpoints.ts:39 ships `legacySupportImpersonate: { method: 'POST', path: '/legacy/support/impersonate' }` and the comment directly above at lines 33-36 states 'The gateway still answers them for old installs; nothing in this build calls them'.

accounts.ts:25 indexes SORT_COLUMNS — a plain object literal at db.ts:17-21 with a live Object.prototype — and the `??` fallback only catches null/undefined; I confirmed in node that sort='constructor'/'toString'/'valueOf'/'hasOwnProperty' each return a prototype member instead of falling back, and that value goes on to sql.unsafe(orderBy) at db.ts:78.

exports.py:31, 46 and 66 write note bodies / docket summaries into csv.writer rows with no leading =,+,-,@,tab guard; QUOTE_ALL only quotes the field, which spreadsheets still evaluate, and the body is free text bounded only by length at repository.py:35-40.

repository.py:87 calls policy.assert_can_write(principal, case) and then line 88 mutates the separately-passed `note`; nothing in the function (or in policy.py) asserts note.case_id == case.id, so write clearance on one matter authorises redaction of a note belonging to another.

entitlements.ts:57 seatsRemaining is exported and grep over pulsegate-api finds no call site; the seats and apiCallsPerDay values from PLAN_LIMITS (entitlements.ts:16-24) are only ever echoed back by entitlementsFor at lines 50-52 for the GET /entitlements route (accounts.ts:31) — insertMember and the batch route never count seats, and rateLimit (middleware.ts:15-31) uses a flat 120/min unrelated to the plan.

The debug task does lack no_log, but rotate-secrets.yml:23 tags it `[never, troubleshoot]`, and Ansible's `never` tag means the task is skipped on an ordinary run and executes only when the operator explicitly asks for that tag — so the playbook does not print the password as asserted.

iam.ts:99 sets Principal { AWS: '*' } on the partnerAnalytics trust policy, with only sts:ExternalId and aws:SecureTransport as conditions (lines 101-104) — no account, ARN or org restriction on who may call sts:AssumeRole.
iam.ts:67-76 builds every task role's assumeRolePolicy with Principal { Service: 'ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com' } and no Condition block at all — no aws:SourceAccount and no aws:SourceArn.

storage.ts:98-104 sets blockPublicAcls and ignorePublicAcls true but blockPublicPolicy false (line 101) and restrictPublicBuckets false (line 103) — the two flags that govern bucket policies — on a bucket that carries a bucket policy at lines 114-132.

Pulumi.staging.yaml:9 sets publicExports true, which storage.ts:42-68 turns into all-four-flags-off public access block plus a Principal '*' GetObject policy, and Pulumi.staging.yaml:12 sets replicateProdExports true, which storage.ts:70-89 turns into the inbound prod replication policy.

auth.ts:99 is `new TextEncoder().encode(process.env.SERVICE_TOKEN_KEY ?? 'local-development-key')`, and that key signs the HS256 service token returned at lines 100-106 with no boot-time check that the variable is set — unlike the client secrets, which are refused when empty at line 96.

stg_payout_events.sql:26 filters `j.created_at > (select coalesce(max(created_at), ...) from {{ this }})`, so a row whose created_at equals the stored maximum is excluded on every later run and never lands; customer_pii_masked.sql:33 uses the same strict `>` on updated_at.

ingest.py:110 returns `bool(message.get("signature")) and message.get("producer") in {...}` — presence only, never an HMAC or key comparison — and consume_batch then builds the dataclass directly at line 123, so the forged doc's acl_groups and tenant skip every DocumentIn validator (ingest.py:35-51).

storage.ts:156-162 sets all four BucketPublicAccessBlock flags false and lines 164-174 attach a Principal '*' s3:GetObject policy on the same bucket; the function is exported and dormant (grep finds no caller in index.ts), but its body is exactly what the assertion describes.

storage.ts:51 and storage.ts:73 both create an aws.s3.BucketPolicy against `bucket: exports_.id`, and Pulumi.staging.yaml:9 and :12 turn both branches on at once — S3 holds a single policy document per bucket, so whichever resource applies last silently replaces the other.

roles/app/tasks/main.yml:49-58 starts the app as a docker container published on 127.0.0.1, then lines 86-110 install and start a second, native systemd copy reading the same app.env, whose LISTEN_ADDR comes from app.env.j2:8 = group_vars/all.yml:19 '0.0.0.0'; the ufw default-deny is applied only to `hosts: bastion` (site.yml:2-6), so appservers and edge run unfirewalled.

exports.py:30-31 writes note.body straight into the CSV row with no leading-formula guard; csv.QUOTE_ALL quotes but does not disarm a value beginning with '=', which Excel/LibreOffice still evaluate on open.

ledger.js:59-65 adjustBalance is a bare upsert with `balance_cents + $2` and no negative-balance check and no maxPostingCents check — both of which its sibling applyPosting enforces at ledger.js:12-14 and 25-28 — and payoutRelease.js:28 is the payout path that calls it.

app.py:27 declares history as `{"type": "array", "maxItems": 20}` with no items schema, and prompt.py:41-42 copies turn["role"] and turn["content"] verbatim into the message list ahead of the user turn, so a caller can insert a system-role message that steers the tool loop built at app.py:101-121.

dim_customer.sql:30-42 keeps email, phone, bank_account and billing address with no age cut-off, and an exhaustive grep of warehouse-dbt for retention/expire/ttl/purge/delete finds only row_security.sql:20's `drop policy` — there are no snapshots, no post-hook deletes and no retention config in dbt_project.yml.

AndroidManifest.xml:47-52 declares `<data android:scheme="https" android:pathPrefix="/r/" />` with no android:host; with no host the path attributes are ignored, so the filter matches every https URI and DeepLinkRouterActivity.routeWeb (DeepLinkRouter.kt:61-64) then loads the attacker-supplied `target` query parameter in the WebView.

store.py:15 constructs QdrantClient(url=config()["store"]["url"], timeout=20) with no api_key, and beacon.yaml:4, :11 and :16 give the store, embeddings and llm endpoints as plain http:// URLs; store.embed (store.py:20-25) likewise posts with no auth header.

data.ts:59-67 creates the analytics replica with publiclyAccessible: true in the public subnet group (line 54-57), and data.ts:71-78 opens the shared network.dbSecurityGroup — the same group the primary uses at line 41 — on tcp/5432 to cidrIpv4 '0.0.0.0/0'.

beacon.yaml:24-27 strips x-beacon-principal, x-beacon-tenant and x-beacon-request-id but not x-beacon-groups, which acl.py:38 reads to build Principal.groups — and those groups are the whole ACL match in acl.group_filter (acl.py:50) and acl.may_read (acl.py:59).

Only handle_payout consults idempotency.lookup before applying (handlers.py:81-84); handle_payout_cancel at handlers.py:91-104 posts the reversal entry with no lookup, handle_payout_reissue at 107-111 calls _apply_payout then only remembers, and handle_refund at 114-127 has no idempotency at all.

repository.py:127-132 takes `principal` and never uses it — no policy.assert_can_read, unlike schedule_export at line 121 — and exports.export_case_bundle opens its own Session(bind=engine) (exports.py:57) outside scoped_session, selecting notes by case_id alone (exports.py:60).

settings.py:47 is a bare literal `demo_api_key: str = "demo-playground-key"` — the only field in the dataclass with no os.getenv override — and app.py:56-57 grants a full Principal to anyone presenting it, so disabling or rotating it requires a code change.

workorders.ts:186 does compile c.req.query('template'), but printQuery is declared .strict() at workorders.ts:164-168 and zValidator('query') is fed every query parameter, so any request carrying `template` fails the unrecognised-keys check and is rejected with 400 before the handler runs — the only value that ever reaches new Function is the DEFAULT_SHEET constant.
